To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

reinforcement of not-responding produces a greater decrease in rate than does reinforcement of responding, and that the effects of reinforcement of responding and not-responding depend on the history of the subject.

reinforcement of not responding produces greater decrements in response rate than does response-independent reinforcement, and that this effect is more pronounced if the time parameter or the nominal frequency of food delivery is considered than if obtained frequency is considered.

the effects of reinforcement of not responding are similar to those of reinforcement of responding when the time parameter of not-responding schedules is considered, but not when the obtained frequency parameter is considered, and that the effects of fixed-time schedules on response rate are similar to those produced by reinforcement of not responding when both the time and obtained frequency parameters are considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of schedules of reinforcement on behavior, and the effects of schedules are considered in relation to the schedules of reinforcement which preceded them.
the effects of response-independent schedules on the rate of key pecking.
the effects of schedules of reinforcement for not responding on the rate of response maintained on a fixed interval schedule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

reinforcement of not responding produces a greater decrease in rate than reinforcement of responding, but that reinforcement of responding is more effective when the rate of reinforcement is considered rather than the nominal rate.
the effects of reinforcement of not responding on response rate are similar to those of response-independent reinforcement, but that the latter schedule has less of an effect.
reinforcement of not responding is more effective than reinforcement of responding in the suppression of key pecking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of a response maintained by food depends on the frequency of food presentation obtained by that response.
reinforcement of not responding produces a decrement in rate which is a function of the time parameter of that schedule.
response-independent reinforcement has the effect of reducing response rate, and that the magnitude of this effect is determined by the frequency of response-independent reinforcement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use reinforcement schedules to change the rate of behavior in ways that are useful to us.
we can use the principles of behavior to help people change their behaviors.
the fixed-time schedule can produce effects similar to those of the differential reinforcement of not responding schedule, but only if the pigeons are experienced with reinforcement for not pecking.
